content: Acetaminophen, Butalbital, and Caffeine is a combination medication prescribed to alleviate tension headaches. It may also be used for other purposes as determined by your doctor. If you have questions about its use, consult your healthcare provider. This medication is available in capsule and tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken every 4 hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more than six tablets or capsules in a single day. If you feel that your symptoms are not adequately controlled, contact your doctor. This medication has the potential to be habit-forming, so do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acetaminophen, butalbital, caffeine, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antidepressants, antihistamines, pain medications, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Be aware that many over-the-counter pain relievers contain acetaminophen, and excessive intake of this drug can be harmful. Inform your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, porphyria, or depression. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. This medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this drug, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. To minimize stomach upset, take this medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, depression, lightheadedness, or confusion. If you experience serious side effects such as a skin rash, itching, or difficulty breathing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to this medication. Do not share this medication with others, as it is a controlled substance. Prescription refills are limited, so consult your pharmacist if you have questions.
